title: Courthouse Wedding in San Diego: Real Cost & Steps (2026)
description: Courthouse wedding in San Diego: $236 in fees: license $129 + ceremony $107, per the county clerk. ID, booking and witness steps. Checked Oct 29, 2026.

answer_html: As of Oct 29, 2026, a courthouse wedding in San Diego costs $236 in official fees: $129 for the public marriage license and $107 for the civil ceremony (San Diego County Assessor/Recorder/County Clerk). You can marry as soon as the license is issued.

facts.quote: License fees are non-refundable.

facts.label: How long the license is valid
facts.display: 90 days, with no extensions; the ceremony must be in California
facts.quote: A marriage license is valid for 90 days with NO extensions. A ceremony must take place within 90 days of the license issuance and within the State of California.

facts.label: Who must attend
facts.display: Both of you, together
facts.quote: Both parties must appear together at their appointment.

facts.label: ID you bring
facts.display: A valid, current government photo ID for each of you (driver's license, passport, military ID or state ID); with an expired ID the license cannot be issued
facts.quote: Both parties must present valid and current government-issued photo ID. / The ID must be current - if it is expired, the marriage license cannot be issued.

facts.label: Age

facts.label: Residency

facts.quote: There is no residency requirement.

facts.label: Language

facts.quote: Both parties must be able to read, speak, and understand English or Spanish.

facts.quote: Must have at least one witness present at the ceremony.

facts.label: Witness, confidential license

facts.quote: No witnesses are required to be present at the ceremony. / Couples must be living together as spouses at the time they apply for the marriage license and must sign under penalty of perjury attesting to that fact.

facts.label: What you cannot bring
facts.display: Floral arrangements, backdrops, arches or furniture, live musicians or amplified music, confetti, flower petals, bird seed or rice, open alcohol (champagne included), anything that needs setup
facts.quote: outside décor and custom setups are not permitted at Recorder/County Clerk ceremony locations. This policy includes, but is not limited to: Floral arrangements or decorations for the arbor or ceremony area Backdrops, arches, or furniture Live musicians or amplified music Tossing materials (such as confetti, flower petals, bird seed, or rice) Open containers of alcohol (including champagne) and alcohol consumption Any equipment or items that require setup or breakdown time

facts.label: After the ceremony
facts.display: Your officiant signs the license and returns it to the office; registering it may take up to 10 business days; a copy is not sent to you automatically
facts.quote: After the ceremony, the marriage license must be signed by your officiant and returned to our office for registration. Registering the license may take up to 10 business days. / One will not automatically be sent to you.

steps: Book an appointment with the San Diego County Clerk, up to 7 weeks ahead; a “License and Ceremony” appointment does both in one visit.
After booking, complete the county's online marriage license application.
Go together, each with a current government photo ID, and pay $129 for a public license or $144 for a confidential one.

Have the civil ceremony ($107) indoors or outdoors in Waterfront Park; a public license needs at least one witness (or the county's, $58). You can marry as soon as the license is issued, and within 90 days.
The signed license is registered within up to 10 business days; order a certified copy ($19) if you need proof of marriage.

faq.q: How much does a courthouse wedding cost in San Diego?
faq.a: As of Oct 29, 2026, the San Diego County Clerk charges $129 for a public marriage license ($144 for a confidential one) and $107 for a civil ceremony: $236 in all, or $251 with a confidential license. A county-provided witness is $58 more, and paying by card adds $2.50.

faq.q: Can you get married at the courthouse in San Diego?
faq.a: In San Diego the County Clerk, not a court, marries you: by appointment only, at the County Administration Center or the Chula Vista, San Marcos or Santee office. At the County Administration Center you can also marry outdoors, in Waterfront Park.

faq.q: How do you get a marriage license in San Diego County?
faq.a: Book an appointment (up to 7 weeks ahead), then fill in the county's online application. Both of you go together, each with a current government photo ID (an expired one is refused), and you must both be 18 or older. The license costs $129 (public) or $144 (confidential) and is valid for 90 days, with no extensions.

faq.q: Can you get married the same day in San Diego?
faq.a: Yes, with a “License and Ceremony” appointment: the county says you can marry as soon as the license is issued. Appointments open up to 7 weeks ahead and fill up quickly, so book early.

faq.q: Do you need a witness for a San Diego courthouse wedding?
faq.a: With a public license, at least one witness must be at the ceremony: bring your own, or the county provides one for $58. A confidential license needs no witness, but you must already live together as spouses to get one.

steps5.text: Up to 7 weeks ahead; slots fill up quickly. Choose a “License and Ceremony” appointment to do both in one visit.

steps5.text: After you book, complete the county's online marriage license application (or bring the printable one).

steps5.title: Get your license
steps5.text: Both of you, together, each with a current government photo ID (an expired ID is refused). $144 if you choose a confidential license.

steps5.title: Say your vows
steps5.text: Indoors at one of the 4 county offices, or outdoors in Waterfront Park at the County Administration Center. A public license needs one witness: bring your own, or the county's is $58.

steps5.text: The license is signed and returned for registration (up to 10 business days). A certified copy is $19 and is not sent to you automatically.

tips.t: At the County Administration Center, outdoor ceremonies take place in Waterfront Park, with no limit on guests. The county may move you to the East Plaza when there is an event in the park, and weather can change the plan.
The county does not allow floral arrangements for the ceremony area, arches or backdrops, live or amplified music, confetti, petals or rice, or open alcohol, champagne included.
The County Administration Center has free underground parking for up to 3 hours during business hours; the garage entrance is on Ash Street.
One Saturday a month, at the Santee office only, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., by appointment. The next dates are November 14 and December 12, 2026.
Indoor rooms hold 20 to 30 guests at the County Administration Center, 15 in Chula Vista and San Marcos and 20 in Santee (per the county's FAQ). A public license needs at least one witness.
A short or midi white dress, a slip dress or a jumpsuit is easy to wear for a county office ceremony and looks great in photos. Bring a light jacket or wrap for the park.
